title: Versions and citation

---

```{r}
#| include: false
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
# Explicit: duckdb's extension autoinstall fails on fresh CI runners.
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; INSTALL json; LOAD json;")
```

OmicIDX publishes three kinds of versions. They hold the same tables in the
same layout; they differ in how long they last and how you use them.
[Releases](../releases.qmd) lists the ones available now.

| Version | Where | Changes? | Kept | Use it by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `latest/` | `https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/` | rebuilt every night | always the newest | querying in place |
| Dated | `https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/v{YYYY-MM-DD}/` | never | 30 days | querying in place |
| Monthly release | HuggingFace dataset [`seandavis/omicidx`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/seandavis/omicidx), git tag `YYYY-MM` | never | long term, with a DOI | downloading, then querying locally |

`latest/` and the dated folders are served for querying in place: DuckDB
`ATTACH`, `read_parquet`, omicidxr, and the [playground](../playground.qmd)
all read them over HTTPS. The monthly releases are the long-term archive and
the version to cite. Download one, then query it locally.

## Which one to use

- **Exploring, or building something that should track NCBI:** use `latest/`.
- **An analysis you'll rerun in the next few weeks:** pin a dated folder.
- **A paper, a shared pipeline, or anything you'll cite:** download a monthly release.

## Pin a dated folder

Replace `latest/` with a date:

```{.sql .no-shell}
SELECT count(*)
FROM read_parquet('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/v2026-10-20/sradb/study.parquet');
```

To see which dates are available, open [Releases](../releases.qmd) or the
[folder listing](https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/). Dated folders older
than 30 days are deleted. Use a monthly release for anything longer.

::: callout-caution
In dated folders published before late October 2026, `omicidx.duckdb` and
`views.sql` point at `latest/`, not at their own folder. For those dates, pin
with `read_parquet` on the dated URLs, as above.
:::

## Use a monthly release

Once a month, one nightly build is copied to the HuggingFace dataset
`seandavis/omicidx` and tagged with its month (e.g. `2026-10`). Files sit at
the repository root in the same layout as R2 (`sra_runs.parquet`,
`sradb/study.parquet`, …).

Download the release with the [`hf` command-line
tool](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/guides/cli) (in
`huggingface_hub`; `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf` runs it without
installing), then query the local files:

```bash
hf download seandavis/omicidx --repo-type dataset --revision 2026-10 \
  --local-dir omicidx-2026-10
duckdb -c "SELECT count(*) FROM 'omicidx-2026-10/sradb/study.parquet'"
```

`--include 'sradb/*'` downloads only some of the files. A [HuggingFace
token](https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens) (`hf auth login`) raises the
download rate limits.

In R, `omicidx_download("2026-10", "omicidx-2026-10.duckdb")` builds a local
DuckDB database from a monthly release and checks its row counts (see
[omicidxr](r-omicidxr.qmd#a-local-copy)). For `latest/` and dated folders,
[`restore.sql`](duckdb-snapshot.qmd#work-offline) does the same from the
command line.

DuckDB can also read a release in place with `hf://` paths, where `@tag` pins
the release:

```{.sql .no-shell}
SELECT count(*)
FROM 'hf://datasets/seandavis/omicidx@2026-10/sradb/study.parquet';
```

That's fine for a quick look, but HuggingFace limits anonymous requests to
3000 per 5 minutes per IP address, and a query can make hundreds, so repeated
queries soon fail with HTTP 429. Download for real work.

## Cite OmicIDX

Each monthly release gets a DOI, minted on HuggingFace. Cite the DOI of the
release you used, which you'll find on the dataset page for that tag. In your
methods, also state the release tag (e.g. `2026-10`).

If you used a dated folder instead, record its URL and the `transform_sha`
and `lake_snapshot_id` from its `manifest.json`. The folder will be gone in
30 days, so a monthly release is the better thing to cite.

## The manifest

Every version has a `manifest.json`:

```bash
curl -s https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json
```

DuckDB reads it directly. The provenance fields of the current `latest/`:

```{sql}
SELECT publish_date, dated_path, transform_sha, lake_snapshot_id
FROM read_json('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json');
```

And the row count of each published table:

```{sql, max.print = 50}
SELECT t.schema, t."table", t.row_count
FROM read_json('https://omicidx.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/manifest.json'),
     unnest(tables) AS u(t)
ORDER BY t.schema, t."table";
```

- `transform_sha` is the commit of the [pipeline code](https://github.com/seandavi/omicidx) that built the tables.
- `lake_snapshot_id` is the snapshot of the internal lake the tables were exported from.
- `tables` gives the row count of each published table. `raw_partition_counts` records how many upstream partitions each source had.
